source.description: One reviewed eight-panel felt-tip marker contact sheet cropped into seven cumulative process frames and one finished master.
source.notes: Keep one face-free open book in a shallow three-quarter view, two page blocks, one center gutter, one visible cover edge, one ribbon bookmark emerging from the gutter, two outer page curls, exactly three stacked lower page-edge bands per side, small open-paper cover highlights, one broken navy shadow, thick imperfect black outlines, saturated raspberry, teal, yellow, and coral marker fills, and no marks on the broad page faces except the visible marker grain itself; no readable text, letters, symbols, labels, arrows, numbers, signature, watermark, sticker border, or badge frame.

process_strategy: Use eight cumulative stages with visibly different drawing jobs: a sparse center-hinge and page-span gesture, two loose page-face silhouettes, complete pencil construction for the thickness cover ribbon curls bands highlights and shadow, full structural ink with coral ribbon, yellow bands and navy shadow, restrained cover hatching, raspberry-and-teal page color, and final reinforcement. Do not front-load the completed book into Step 1; reserve every overlap in Step 3 before keeper ink so no established line is erased later.

final_elements.name: pale center-hinge and page-span gesture
final_elements.description: A few very pale pencil strokes establish only the center hinge, the shallow spread angle, two page-span arcs, and four outer corner points; there is no closed book contour, thickness, ribbon, curl, band, highlight, shadow, ink, or color yet.

final_elements.name: rough two-page page-face silhouette and center gutter
final_elements.description: Loose pencil contours turn the gesture into exactly two broad page faces meeting at one V-shaped center gutter while leaving the lower thickness, cover, ribbon, curls, bands, highlights, shadow, ink, and color absent.

final_elements.name: page-block thickness cover ribbon curl band highlight and shadow construction
final_elements.description: Pale pencil completes the lower page-block thickness, visible cover lip, one ribbon footprint, two outer curl silhouettes, exactly three lower-band routes per side, small cover-highlight gaps, and one broken shadow footprint around the unchanged page faces and gutter.

final_elements.name: full black structural ink and one coral ribbon bookmark
final_elements.description: Imperfect black felt-tip traces the established page, gutter, thickness, cover, ribbon, curl, band, highlight, and shadow boundaries, and the single ribbon receives its first coral marker fill without changing the geometry.

final_elements.name: three yellow lower page-edge bands per side small cover highlights and broken navy shadow
final_elements.description: Exactly three stacked curved bands inside each lower page-block thickness receive warm-yellow marker, small open-paper highlight gaps remain on the cover edge, and one broken deep-navy shadow grounds the book without adding marks to the broad page faces.

final_elements.name: restrained cover-edge hatching and deeper existing navy shadow
final_elements.description: Short handmade hatching deepens only the established outer cover edges and the same broken navy shadow while every previously inked boundary and color area remains unchanged.

final_elements.name: raspberry and teal page-face and cover marker fills
final_elements.description: Raspberry fills the left blank page face and related cover plane, teal fills the right blank page face and related cover plane, and both retain visible marker streaks while the established yellow bands, coral ribbon, navy shadow, black outlines, and open-paper highlights remain unchanged.

overlap_reservations.background_lines_stop_before: The Step 3 gutter and page-block lines stop at the ribbon footprint, the cover edge stops at the ribbon exit, and all page-layer curves stop before both outer curl silhouettes.

overlap_reservations.background_lines_stop_before: Marker fills stop around the reserved cover-edge highlight gaps, all six bands stay inside the lower page-block thickness rather than migrating onto the broad page faces, and the broken shadow stops at the book and ribbon silhouettes.

final_step.step_name: Turn the page on the finish
final_step.visible_job: Only strengthens selected established black edges, evens existing marker fills, clarifies the same two paper highlights, and deepens the existing edge hatching and broken shadow without changing the book, page count, ribbon, curls, layer-curve counts, palette, or composition.

rejection_checks: The Step 1 hinge gesture and Step 2 page-face silhouettes must resolve into the same shallow three-quarter book, crop, spread angle, center gutter, and scale used by Steps 3-8; do not morph or recenter the subject.

Do not front-load the finished book: Step 1 must remain a sparse gesture, Step 2 must add only two page-face silhouettes and the gutter, and Step 3 must make the clearly larger jump to thickness, cover, ribbon, curls, bands, highlights, and shadow construction.

Keep one open book, two page blocks, one center gutter, one ribbon bookmark, two outer page curls, exactly three lower page-edge bands per side, the small cover-edge highlight gaps, and one broken shadow after those elements appear in Step 3.
The gutter angle, page widths, cover thickness, ribbon route, and curl positions may not drift between panels.

The ribbon must occupy only its reserved gutter route, all six page bands must stay inside the lower thickness and stop before both curl silhouettes, marker fills must stop around the cover-edge highlight gaps, and the shadow must stop at the book and ribbon.
Do not add readable words, letters, symbols, page numbers, character face, glasses, pen, flowers, coffee, hands, second book, sticker border, badge frame, label, arrow, signature, or watermark.
The final panel may not introduce a page block, gutter, cover edge, bookmark, page curl, lower page band, highlight, hatch cluster, shadow shape, or color area.
The finish must retain visible felt-tip streaks and imperfect handmade edges rather than vector-clean clip art, polished publishing graphics, glossy AI poster art, or rasterized vector drawing.
